comments.body: Done in 1ec6614e: --as naming the caller's own pane (callsign or id) means the caller's own participant, whatever it joined as; another pane's callsign and an address-less script are still refused name_of_pane. Stores that already forked a participant are not repaired (indistinguishable from a deliberate join --name).
comments.author: Alexander Terp

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Seen 2026-11-08 00:05 on the Mac mini, in an agent-engine parallel-work round. The integrator, pane lark, ran `muster msg wait --as lark --timeout 3000` in the background so a worker's post would wake it. From then on Muster treated `lark` as a participant separate from the pane:

- @muster sent four 'went idle without posting to you' notices in new groups `lark+yarrow-2`, `lark+vole-2`, `glacier+lark-2` and `lark+rudder-2`, three of them about workers that had posted their plans to lark minutes earlier in the original groups, whose members are the panes.
- `muster msg post --group lark+yarrow --to yarrow ...` from lark's session then failed with 'lark is not in lark+yarrow; join it'. The session now resolved to the name `lark` rather than the pane, so every later post went to a -2 group, and workers had to post to the -2 groups to reach it.

Expected: `--as <name>`, where the name is a live pane's callsign (here the caller's own), resolves to that pane, or is refused with a message saying why. The idle-without-posting notice should also count posts to the pane under either identity.

Related: a_2o5StNxnb, where `--as @human` takes over the human's identity in the same way. From tooling feedback a_2vzq0Nd1b.
title: `msg wait --as <own callsign>` makes a second participant, and the pane's later posts go to new groups
